clue.text: Primate, one replacing duke in cricket ground

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes the place of another inside the word for the cricket ground

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
one as the Roman numeral I
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A monkey wanders onto a cricket ground and takes a duke's place.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the home of English cricket in London; swap its D for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The loris is a small, slow-moving nocturnal primate of southern Asia, so it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Party passionate about current venture initially requiring many workers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the passionate word wraps around what follows

parts.note: Labour is a British political party
intense means passionate
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of venture

explanation.surface: A political party is fired up about a new business that needs a big workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour-intensive task or industry is one that depends on lots of human effort rather than machines.

clue.text: Priest captivated by churchgoer's saintly memorial

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive, so the priest sits inside the churchgoer

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, a churchgoer
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest is enchanted by a worshipper's memorial to a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a body part or belonging of a saint kept as an object of veneration.

clue.text: Main sentence identifying cormorant, for example

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: The key sentence in a text picks out the cormorant as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for the sea; doing bird is British slang for serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a fish-eating diver of coasts, one example of a bird living by the ocean.

clue.text: Time to tie up outside club, securing old vessel

indicators.note: outside puts the word for tie up around the letter for time

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: securing means the word for club holds the letter for old inside it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone moors a boat and grabs a club, seemingly preparing an old craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' is a sporting club, not a society; the clue holds two separate containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorboat is a kind of vessel driven by an engine, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Shabby-sounding carriage?

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is pronounced like the one for shabby

parts.note: mean can describe something shabby and poor

explanation.surface: A shabby-sounding horse-drawn coach, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle; here it is how a person carries themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or manner, and carriage likewise means posture or deportment.

clue.text: Swiss hero absorbing a tirade over a lively dance

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the hero's name surrounds the next words

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero
taken as written
a rant is a tirade
taken as written

explanation.surface: William Tell sits through a furious tirade, then dances.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part on top of the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast, whirling Italian folk dance from southern Italy.

clue.text: Right to retain the last word about one's clothing

indicators.note: to retain means to keep hold of, so the abbreviation for right encloses the rest

parts.note: Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the last word goes around the letter for one

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Insisting on the final say about what one wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The containers nest: the numeral goes inside the prayer's last word, and that whole goes inside the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary, old-fashioned word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Forthright Open University man accepting special post

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the university and man surround the rest
special suggests a made-over version, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: OU is the Open University
taken as written, then rearranged
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A blunt academic at the Open University takes up a special job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' looks like it describes the post, but it signals a rearrangement of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forthright says plainly what they think, which is what being outspoken means.

clue.text: Old Icelandic character appearing personally, a constant irritation

parts.note: thorn is the old runic letter þ, still used in Icelandic
to appear in the flesh is to be there in person

explanation.surface: An old Icelandic figure who keeps turning up in person is a constant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of an alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from St Paul's letters, means a persistent source of annoyance or trouble.

clue.text: Singer, a large youth overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by suggests being swamped, so these letters sit inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A big young man gets drunk while singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a performer of ballads, so a particular kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Prelude written in fortnight going west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading from right to left
written in says the letters are already sitting inside the following word

parts.note: the letters inside the word, which are then read backwards

explanation.surface: A musical prelude composed within two weeks of heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an informal word for an introduction, the opening passage of a piece.

clue.text: Young rogue backing game with companion taking part

indicators.note: backing means the letters for the game run backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
someone taking part is in

explanation.surface: A young scoundrel supports a game played with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a mischievous, often scruffy child, which matches a youthful little rascal.

clue.text: Support from beneath, subject to identification

parts.note: under in the sense of subject to, as in under orders
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: Something holds a thing up from below and is subject to checking ID.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is literally to prop up a structure with foundations below it.

clue.text: US composer's endless ambition to produce close harmony

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the word for ambition

parts.note: Samuel Barber was an American composer, with the possessive s
a hope is an ambition

explanation.surface: An American composer's restless drive yields tight harmonies.
explanation.walkthrough: Barber is best known for his Adagio for Strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of unaccompanied singing in close four-part harmony.

clue.text: Pressing news outlets to probe unusual item

indicators.note: to probe means to go inside, so the news outlets sit within the other letters
unusual means the following word is arranged in an odd way

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the media are the outlets for news

explanation.surface: Urgent news stories are sent to dig into a strange item.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is urgent, needing attention at once, which is what immediate means.

clue.text: Many initially help, engaging a good physio

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, so the word for help holds the next letters
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of many
to assist is to help
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Lots of people start by helping, hiring a decent physiotherapist.
explanation.definitionFit: A massagist is a person who gives massages, and a physio treats patients by similar manipulation.

clue.text: Warning given by small number touring Oklahoma

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the number wraps around the state

parts.note: ten is a small number
OK is the postal abbreviation for Oklahoma

explanation.surface: A small group on a tour of Oklahoma issues a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or omen, and in older use a portent that warns of what is coming.

clue.text: Experience discrimination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to have a brief experience of something, as in a sample of freedom
second meaning: refined judgement in matters of style

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a phrase about suffering prejudice; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to get a sample of something; as a noun it means discerning aesthetic judgement.

clue.text: Shrub ambassador introduced to new padre

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the ambassador goes into the other letters
new means a fresh version, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat is introduced to a newly arrived army chaplain beside a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedra is a genus of jointed, almost leafless shrubs, the source of the drug ephedrine.

clue.text: Aggressive man in church trapping female bird

indicators.note: trapping means holding something enclosed, so the female letter sits within the rest

parts.note: a bull of a man is big and aggressive
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A violent man in a church catches a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In church' reads as a location, but both words supply letters, and the female letter is trapped among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfinch is a stocky European finch with a rosy breast, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Frenzied Italian brought up in country, mostly

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the shortened country
mostly means not quite all, so the country loses its final letter

parts.note: France is a country

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian raised abroad, more or less, is in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic describes wild, desperate agitation, the same out-of-control state as frenzied.

clue.text: Boring type carrying articles for old animal minder

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the articles go inside the boring type

parts.note: a nerd is a dull, boring person
a and the are the two articles in English

explanation.surface: A dull person brings some items for an elderly zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' are the grammatical ones, A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, so a neatherd was a cowherd, a historical keeper of livestock.

clue.text: A lot of people I originally found in a mountainous region

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd
taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of found

explanation.surface: A crowd, and the speaker, turned up somewhere in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a single upland block, hence a hilly area.

clue.text: Drunkard pinching a bishop's footwear

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the drunkard encloses the next letters

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A drunk steals a bishop's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog worn by peasants in France, so a type of shoe.

clue.text: A graduate in education, retired possibly

parts.note: taken as written
a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A teacher with an education degree has perhaps given up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work; here it means having gone to bed, hence the question of possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to sleep for the night, and someone abed is lying there sleeping.

clue.text: Retired woman concealing worry about written work

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for woman is read backwards
about means turned round, so the word for worry runs backwards
concealing means hiding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
to ail is to trouble or worry

explanation.surface: A woman in retirement hides her anxiety about something she has written.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned round before one goes inside the other; 'Retired' looks like a description of the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem about the siege of Troy, a famous literary composition.

clue.text: Fit to be lived in by husband having a few talents?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
read as a bit able, someone with a few skills

explanation.surface: A husband with modest talents sounds like a mixed blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: having a few talents makes you a bit able.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitable describes a place in good enough condition for people to make a home there.

clue.text: Caught in hospital department and ticked off

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
to be rapped is to be reprimanded or told off

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hospital ward gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticked off' means scolded here, not marked with a tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrapped means snared or trapped, the same state as being caught.

clue.text: Hear possibly bawdy round

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make out what someone said, an example of hearing
second meaning: a round for several voices, historically often with ribald words

explanation.walkthrough: A round is a song where voices enter in turn; the catches of the 17th century were famously rude.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to perceive a remark, and the noun is an old type of comic part-song sung in turn.
